correctness.rationale: For all a,c>0 and 0<h<1, the Zak symbol is the sum of two uniformly convergent geometric series. A zero is equivalent to an explicit real scalar equation Q(phi)=0, with Q(0)>0. Exact minimization of F=cos(phi)-r^2 cos(theta-phi) gives the two piecewise formulas; the discriminants determine reciprocal amplitude roots. Monotonicity/unimodality counts all zeros including edge/tangency. Denominators are uniformly separated from zero, so absence/presence of zeros is exactly frame/nonframe. Direct standalone code passed 497 diagnostic assertions; finite tests are not the infinite proof.

evidence: At h=1/2 the new c-interval reduces algebraically to [(1-r)/(1+r),(1+r)/(1-r)], exactly the previously published special case; that limit is explicitly not new.
When h<1/2 and r<cos(pi*h), the interval vanishes for all c>0; when h>1/2 a nonframe interval persists for every r>0. Neither behavior can be deduced solely from h=1/2.
For h>1/2 an interior Zak contact occurs at each c-boundary, and one or two interior zeros occur according to a second exact inequality, whereas h=1/2 has edge contacts and one interior zero.
